OSS VAT Explained: the EU One-Stop Shop for Small Sellers

Last updated: 2026-08-23 · Source: European Commission TEDB · 6 min read

If you sell to consumers in other EU countries — on Etsy, Shopify, or as a freelancer selling downloads — the EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) lets you report that VAT through a single return in your home country instead of registering for VAT in every country you sell into.

What the OSS is

The One-Stop Shop is an EU-wide filing scheme for cross-border business-to-consumer (B2C) sales. You register once, charge the buyer's country VAT rate on each sale, and declare it all on one OSS return. It most commonly covers B2C goods and digital services — for example an Etsy printable sold from Germany to a buyer in France (20% standard rate).

Who it suits

It suits small sellers with cross-border consumer sales who would otherwise face a registration in each buyer's country. Separate local registrations are still needed in some cases — for example if you hold stock in another country — so confirm your position with an accountant. Sales to VAT-registered businesses in another EU country are generally handled differently (often zero-rated with reverse charge).

Which rate to charge on each sale

Under OSS you still charge the buyer's country rate — the scheme changes where you report, not which rate applies. Look up the destination in the full EU VAT rates table (all 27 countries + UK): for instance Germany charges 19%, Ireland 23%, and Hungary 27%. Then compute the VAT-inclusive price with the free VAT calculator, or check how to reverse-calculate VAT when a supplier quotes you gross prices.

How to get started

Registration runs through your own country's tax portal, and returns are typically filed quarterly. Keep per-country sales records so each line of the return matches the rate you charged. Your accountant can confirm whether your products and customer types qualify before your first filing.
